major_features: Raw socket capture and injection interface
Protocol-specific header field mutation engine
Checksum corruption and sequence number randomization
Stateful tracking of TCP connection lifecycle
Automated reproduction of crash-inducing packet sequences
Real-time packet capture and logging to pcap format
Configurable mutation rate and protocol segment selection
Deterministic test suite for kernel panic detection
candidate_ideas.name: Kernel-Level Packet Fuzzer
candidate_ideas.pain: Lack of deterministic, stateful protocol fuzzer that can inject malformed packets into a local loopback interface.
candidate_ideas.problem: Network stacks are often tested with valid traffic, leaving edge-case vulnerabilities in TCP/IP parsing logic undiscovered.
candidate_ideas.solution: A C11 network fuzzer that crafts arbitrary Ethernet/IP/TCP frames, performs checksum manipulation, and monitors kernel-space socket state for crashes or hangs.
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic replay of failed test sequences; validation of packet integrity against RFC standards; automated detection of socket-level resource leaks.

major_features: Custom B+Tree implementation for on-disk metadata
Page-aligned binary serialization for index nodes
Direct ByteBuffer-based I/O for zero-copy reads
Atomic page splitting and merging logic
Background LSM compaction worker using Virtual Threads
Bloom filter integration for index-level lookups
WAL-based recovery for incomplete page writes
Integrated performance monitor for I/O latency tracking
candidate_ideas.name: LSM-Tree Metadata Indexer
candidate_ideas.pain: Difficulty in visualizing and optimizing the interaction between MemTable flushes and tiered storage compaction.
candidate_ideas.problem: Large-scale LSM trees suffer from metadata overhead and slow point-lookups when index blocks are not perfectly aligned with disk pages.
candidate_ideas.solution: A Java 21 storage engine focusing on a custom B+Tree-on-LSM hybrid index, optimized for high-throughput metadata lookups with zero-copy I/O.
candidate_ideas.verification: Cross-verification of index state vs. physical byte-offset map; stress testing with non-sequential key insertions to ensure tree balance.

major_features: DIMACS file format parser for CNF instances
DPLL algorithm with unit propagation
Pure literal elimination optimization
Conflict-driven clause learning (CDCL) engine
Backtracking search with variable heuristic branching
Interactive proof-trace generator for logic validation
Memory-efficient clause database management
Deterministic test harness for edge-case unsatisfiability
candidate_ideas.name: Symbolic Logic Solver
candidate_ideas.pain: Existing solvers are too heavy to embed directly into lightweight analysis pipelines for local code verification.
candidate_ideas.problem: Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solvers are often treated as black boxes, making them difficult to integrate into custom static analysis tools.
candidate_ideas.solution: A pure Python 3.12 DPLL-based SAT solver featuring a custom expression parser, clause learning, and conflict-driven clause analysis.
candidate_ideas.verification: Validation against standard DIMACS CNF benchmarks; performance profiling on unsatisfiable vs. satisfiable problem sets.

major_features: Gossip-based peer discovery and state propagation
Vector clock implementation for causal ordering
Lock-free priority queue for local event management
Virtual Thread-based network communication layer
Deterministic event execution logic for task triggers
Fault-tolerant membership management via failure detectors
Binary serialization for event message payloads
Network delay injection harness for consistency testing
candidate_ideas.name: Distributed Event Scheduler
candidate_ideas.pain: Lack of a lightweight, decentralized scheduling mechanism that guarantees event ordering without a central master node.
candidate_ideas.problem: Coordinating scheduled tasks across multiple isolated nodes is prone to race conditions and clock drift.
candidate_ideas.solution: A Java 21 decentralized event scheduler using a custom gossip protocol and vector clocks to achieve consensus on task execution times.
candidate_ideas.verification: Simulation of network partitions to ensure event consistency; stress testing clock drift scenarios to verify causality preservation.

major_features: Recursive-descent parser for custom language grammar
Intermediate Representation (IR) generation with SSA form
Register allocation using graph coloring algorithm
Custom bytecode instruction set design
Disassembler for human-readable bytecode inspection
Static analysis pass for type and scope checking
Memory-mapped bytecode execution buffer
Comprehensive test suite for malformed syntax handling
candidate_ideas.name: JIT-Ready Bytecode Compiler
candidate_ideas.pain: The gap between high-level ASTs and low-level machine code is too large, hiding register allocation and stack management details.
candidate_ideas.problem: Compilers often emit raw machine code that is difficult to introspect or optimize dynamically without a JIT layer.
candidate_ideas.solution: A C11 compiler front-end that transforms a custom high-level language into an intermediate register-based bytecode, ready for a JIT backend.
candidate_ideas.verification: Verification of bytecode correctness via a reference interpreter; exhaustive testing of register allocation bounds.

known_limitations: Gemini discovery reasons from model knowledge; the factory does not claim live market research or verified market demand.

A passing systems release proves the generated source compiled or byte-compiled and its factory-required unit/integration suites passed; it does not by itself prove production-scale reliability, security certification, or benchmark superiority.
Generated systems projects intentionally use standard-library-only Java 21, C11, or Python 3.12 profiles so validation can be deterministic and does not depend on unverifiable third-party packages.

Hard projects are scoped implementations of real mechanisms, not claims of complete compatibility with Redis, full SQL standards, industrial compilers, or frontier machine-learning systems unless the tests and documentation explicitly demonstrate that scope.
